script: [serious] The U.S. Army fought Hitler with balloons. In 1944, about eleven hundred American soldiers, many of them recruited from art schools and ad agencies, went to war with an army of fakes. Inflatable tanks. Fake artillery. Giant speakers blasting recorded sounds of troops and construction into the night. Fake radio traffic. They pretended to be units that weren't there, so the real ones could strike somewhere else. On their final mission, at the Rhine, they impersonated about forty thousand men with more than six hundred inflatable vehicles, and drew German forces away from the real crossing. Among them were a future fashion designer, Bill Blass, and the painter Ellsworth Kelly. Then they were ordered to stay silent. Their story stayed classified for decades. They are credited with saving thousands of lives. In 2024, they received the Congressional Gold Medal. Send this to someone who thinks wars are only won with weapons. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number sixteen. A new file every day.
